provenance: Sizing figures below are COMPUTED from the stated formula, not measured benchmarks. They are deliberately conservative so a recommendation that says 'fits' actually fits. Verify a tag with `ollama show <tag>` before relying on it.

formula.explanation: usable = total_ram - os_reserve[platform]. A model fits when weights + runtime_overhead_gb + kv_cache_gb_per_4k_ctx <= usable, where weights = params_b * bytes_per_param[quant]. Figures assume CPU/unified memory; discrete GPU VRAM substitutes for system RAM on the weights term, which is why a 16 GB machine with an 8 GB GPU behaves like a larger box.

tiers.label: 4 GB
tiers.summary: Below the practical floor for a general chat model on Windows. Sub-1B models and 1-bit (BitNet) builds only, and expect swapping. Treat local inference as experimental at this tier and use a hosted API for real work.

tiers.label: 6 GB
tiers.summary: Runs 0.3B-1B assistants for autocomplete, classification, and extraction. Not a coding model. Close your browser first.

tiers.label: 8 GB
tiers.summary: The first genuinely useful tier. 3-4B Q4 models handle summarisation, rewriting, structured extraction and light code assistance.

tiers.label: 12 GB
tiers.summary: 4B models run with room to spare; 12-14B Q4 fits but leaves little for context. Good general-purpose local tier.

tiers.label: 16 GB
tiers.summary: 12-14B Q4 with real context length, or 4B at high quantisation with long context. This is the sweet spot for local coding help.

tiers.label: 24 GB
tiers.summary: 27B-class Q4 models fit, plus a separate embedding model for RAG running alongside.

tiers.label: 32 GB
tiers.summary: 27-32B Q4 with long context, or a 14B model plus embeddings, reranker and a vector store, all resident at once.

models.use: Classification, tagging, tiny extraction. Not conversational.
1-bit CPU-only inference. The one credible option at 4-6 GB; needs bitnet.cpp, not Ollama.
models.why_special: 1.58-bit weights make this far smaller than its 2.4B parameter count implies; the generic q4 formula overestimates it.

models.use: Reasoning-tuned small model. Strong instruction following for its size.
General assistant with vision input. Good default at 8 GB.
Capable general model; handles multi-step instructions and code review.
Best Microsoft open-weight reasoning model for a 16 GB machine.
Largest Gemma that fits a consumer box. Genuine coding assistance.
RAG embeddings. Runs alongside a chat model at any tier from 8 GB up.
